items.title: D6 e-invoice: optional BG-23 VAT breakdown validation (EN 16931 BR-CO-14 + BR-CO-17)
items.evidence: PR(this cycle): runtime/core/einvoice-validator.ts — adds optional EN 16931 BG-23 VAT-breakdown validation to validateInvoice. BR-CO-17 (per category): BT-117 tax == round(BT-116 taxable × rateBps/10000), computed EXACTLY in BigInt (rateBps = basis points, 10000=100%, 20%=>2000, 5.5%=>550, consistent with the codebase). BR-CO-14: Σ category tax == BT-110 total VAT (exact via economic-unit), computed only when every entry well-formed. OPTIONAL: validated only when inv.vatBreakdown present; absence is not an error (no regression to the valid path, the parser->validate path, or the export round-trip — BG-23 is not emitted/parsed yet, KNOWN_GAP). FAIL-CLOSED: non-integer taxable/tax or missing/negative/non-safe-int rateBps => amount-format HIGH, entry not summed (no silent rounding, no partial trust). Grounded in EN 16931 (standards integration per mandate §6). Tests (einvoice-validator.test.ts, 16; +5): valid breakdown; BR-CO-17 1-cent mismatch=>HIGH; BR-CO-14 sum mismatch=>HIGH with NO spurious BR-CO-17; non-integer=>amount-format HIGH. INDEPENDENT AUDIT: initial REJECT — a real FAIL-OPEN: EN 16931 permits negative BT-116 (credit notes) but the +5000/10000 BigInt division truncates toward zero, mis-rounding every negative-taxable entry by 1 cent (a wrong credit-note breakdown passed valid; a correct one was wrongly rejected). FIXED: round half-AWAY-from-zero symmetrically (round the magnitude, re-apply sign) + added a negative/credit-note regression test (assertion 16); empirically swept neg/pos/tie cases all correct. Re-verified. Gate: validator 16, tsc 0, build OK, full test:report 201/201 @ workers=2. No new primitive (composes economic-unit).

items.title: Bound O(n^2) DoS in classifyObjective negation scan via a local negation look-back window (no input truncation)

items.evidence: PR(this cycle): runtime/core/code-execution.ts — closed a reproduced ARBITRARY-FILE-WRITE security defect. ROOT CAUSE: the SQL checker ran sqlite3.connect(':memory:').executescript(open(f).read()) verbatim ⇒ a reviewed .sql containing "ATTACH DATABASE '<path>' AS x; CREATE TABLE x.t..." or "VACUUM INTO '<path>'" CREATED that file on disk. REPRODUCED end-to-end via the real CLI: an out-of-project secret appeared verbatim in the evidence. FIX: checkTsProject's defaultRunner now runs `node <tsc>` CONFINED in bubblewrap — binds ONLY system code dirs (/usr,/lib,/lib64,/bin,/sbin ro), the typescript package dir (ro), and the project at a FIXED /project path (ro); --unshare-all --clearenv --die-with-parent --new-session; --noEmit forced (overrides a hostile tsconfig emit); tsconfig must live inside projectDir (else BLOCKED). An out-of-project reference now fails to resolve (TS6053/TS2307) with NO content leak; legit clean project still PASS, real type error still FAIL with in-project diagnostics (no over-block). items.title: CRITICAL: bash-command-governor sandbox did --ro-bind / / ⇒ every allowlisted read command read ANY host file (and /proc/1/environ leaked the governor's env/API key); confined to an allowlist
items.evidence: PR(this cycle, branch excellence/bash-governor-sandbox-confinement-20261030 stacked on F2b 81fd2dc): runtime/core/bash-command-governor.ts + runtime/core/bash-command-governor.test.ts (already gated — no package.json change). THREAT (found by a fresh security recon, PROVEN, CRITICAL): sandboxRun built its bwrap argv with `--ro-bind / /` — the ENTIRE host root read-only — so every SAFE_READONLY command (cat/head/tail/stat/wc/file/readlink/realpath/nl) executed by the production 'Governed Bash/Linux Command' capability (objectiveId BASH_COMMAND*, execute:true) read ANY host file with NO authorization gate (action-gate ALLOWs READ/LOW observational). Reproduced: `cat /etc/passwd` → root:x:0:0:…; `cat /etc/hostname` → the host name (no secret-keyword to even trigger the SECRET_PATTERNS blocklist); `cat ~/.bashrc` → a live ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (masked only incidentally by a name-based redactor). The only boundary was SECRET_PATTERNS, a trivially-incomplete literal-substring blocklist — contradicting both this file's own 'genuine isolation' claim and the provider-sandbox doctrine ('NEVER --ro-bind / /'). FIX: replace the whole-root bind with an ALLOWLIST (provider-sandbox posture): system CODE dirs (/usr,/lib,/lib64,/bin,/sbin ro, existing-only) + the mission's repo realpath(process.cwd()) ro + a fresh --proc under --unshare-all's PID ns + --dev + tmpfs /tmp + writable /tmp/work; confidential trees (/etc, /home beyond repo, /root, /var) simply unbound ⇒ unreadable. TWO INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL AUDITS (BROKEN→fix→REJECT→fix→ACCEPT): audit #1 confirmed the file-read closed for every path vector but DEMONSTRATED a NEW leak — `cat /proc/1/environ` returned bwrap's own PID-1 monitor environ, which inherited the governor process's uncleared env (real API key + SSH_CLIENT + session id), because spawnSync('bwrap',…) passed no env override (--clearenv only scrubs the CHILD). CLOSED (audit-recommended, applied): spawn bwrap with a cleared env:{PATH} AND prepend --as-pid-1 (the sandboxed command becomes PID 1; no monitor). Re-audit #2 ⇒ ACCEPT: /proc/1/environ now exposes only PATH/HOME/PWD (proven STRUCTURAL, not redaction-luck, by reproducing the pre-fix leak via raw bwrap — the real secrets appeared without the fix, gone with it ⇒ the new assertions are non-vacuous); /proc/1/{cmdline,cwd,status,root}, /proc/mounts expose only sandbox/structure (no secret, no host root); original host reads still closed (/etc/passwd,/etc/hostname,scratchpad-secret,~/.bashrc,/root,/var all no-content); --as-pid-1 did NOT break the --info-fd launched handshake (echo hi EXECUTED exit0; md5sum unknown⇒SANDBOX_OBSERVED); NO over-block (absolute repo read + echo + stat /usr/bin/node all exit0); secret-boundary pre-exec block unchanged (/etc/shadow, ~/.ssh/id_rsa ⇒ HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED); fail-closed on bwrap-absent ⇒ SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE, never an unconfined spawn; symlink-in-repo/.. traversal cannot leak content (no /etc node exists in the namespace). +6 non-vacuous gated assertions in bash-command-governor.test.ts (59→65: /etc/passwd+/etc/hostname no-leak, repo-read OK, /usr OK, /proc/1/environ + /proc/self/environ no host env). Gate: tsc 0, build 0, full regression 235/235, 0 stale. Register 94 ACCEPTED. RESIDUALS (documented, non-blocking): /proc/mounts discloses the repo's own absolute host path (structure, not a secret); the repo tree is readable inside the sandbox by design (the legitimate mission read scope); buildRedactor remains a name-based log scrubber (not relied on for confinement now that it is structural); a governed command can no longer read arbitrary SYSTEM config outside /usr,/lib,… (e.g. /etc/os-release) — if a specific mission needs one, that is a narrow allowlist follow-on, not a reopening of host-wide read. Integration: stacked C→2A→2B→F3→F1→F2→F2b→S1; NOT merged (gh-auth gate).

items.title: HIGH: code-review Go/Rust checkers leaked arbitrary host-file content (cgo #include / Rust include! incl. macro-aliasing) into review evidence; Go CGO_ENABLED=0 + rustc bwrap-confined
items.evidence: PR(this cycle, branch excellence/code-exec-go-rust-fileread-20261030 stacked on S1 95be922): runtime/core/code-execution.ts + runtime/core/code-execution.test.ts (already gated — no package.json change). THREAT (found by a fresh security recon, PROVEN, HIGH — the Go/Rust analogue of F3's /// <reference>): runSyntaxCheck ran `go build`/`rustc` on a REVIEWED (untrusted) source in a mkdtemp, but two compiler features read files OUTSIDE it and echoed their CONTENT into diagnostics ⇒ into the code-review `evidence`: Go cgo `/* #include "/abs/host/file" */ import "C"` (gcc echoes the included file) and Rust `include!/include_str!/include_bytes!`/`#[path]` (rustc echoes the included file). Reproduced end-to-end (planted secret appeared verbatim). FIX (Go): add CGO_ENABLED=0 to the Go spec env ⇒ cgo disabled ⇒ an `import "C"` file is excluded by build constraints before gcc runs. FIX (Rust): a literal-form regex guard (BLOCKED for include!/include_str!/include_bytes!/#[path]) AS DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH, PLUS — because the first audit proved the regex is bypassable by macro ALIASING (`use std::include as x; x!("/abs")`, which rustc genuinely executes) — the rustc subprocess now runs FILESYSTEM-CONFINED in bubblewrap (confine:true on the Rust spec ⇒ defaultRunner binds ONLY system code dirs /usr,/lib,/lib64,/bin,/sbin + the workspace at its real path; cleared bwrap env + --as-pid-1; fail-closed BLOCKED if bwrap absent) so NO inclusion — aliased or not — can resolve a host path. TWO INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL AUDITS (BROKEN→regex-fix→REJECT→confinement→ACCEPT): audit #1 confirmed Go closed + literal Rust refused but DEMONSTRATED the alias bypass leaking a real file ⇒ REJECT; audit #2 (after confinement) ⇒ ACCEPT: the exact alias bypass + core::include + aliased include_str!/include_bytes! + mod/re-export + macro_rules wrappers ALL FAIL with 'couldn't read … No such file' (file not in the mount namespace), zero content leak; /etc/passwd via alias unreadable; env!/option_env! never surface a value; proc-macro/build.rs never run (bare rustc, not cargo) ⇒ external crate fails closed; Go cgo re-confirmed closed; legit Go + legit Rust NOT over-blocked (PASS); fail-closed on bwrap-absent verified by code; non-vacuous (an unconfined alias-include of a bound /usr file echoes raw bytes — the mechanism that would leak the test marker without confinement). Residual-2 from audit #2 (the fix conditionally bound ~/.rustup/~/.cargo, which could expose ~/.cargo/credentials.toml on a rustup host) CLOSED post-audit by dropping those binds (no-op on this system-rustc host; rustup-only hosts ⇒ fail-closed BLOCKED since the proxy isn't on the restricted PATH) — re-verified identical behavior (aliased FAIL/no-leak, legit PASS, 95/95). +8 non-vacuous gated assertions (code-execution.test 87→95: Rust include!/_str/_bytes/#[path] BLOCKED + legit-not-overblocked + Go CGO_ENABLED=0 spec + confine:true spec + REAL confined-rustc aliased-include no-leak [gated on rustc+bwrap]). Gate: tsc 0, build 0, full regression 235/235, 0 stale. Register 95 ACCEPTED. RESIDUALS (documented, non-blocking): confined rustc can still read PUBLIC system files under /usr (e.g. /usr/bin/go ELF bytes) — non-sensitive, a 'trusted-system-files-disclosable' boundary, flag if /usr/local ever stages secrets; the F3 TS single-file path (code-execution TS spec) remains oracle-only (F3b follow-on — could adopt the same confine:true). items.title: S3b: mission-ledger.recordMission write is now CRASH-ATOMIC (temp+rename); honestly scoped — does NOT fix the concurrent lost-update (documented, non-reachable)
items.evidence: PR(this cycle, branch excellence/validation-deliverable-target-allowlist-20261030, committed on top of F1c a68cd01): runtime/core/mission-ledger.ts. Follow-on to S3's documented structural note. THREAT addressed: recordMission did `fs.writeFileSync(LEDGER_FILE, …)` directly to the target ⇒ a crash/interrupt MID-WRITE could leave a torn/half-written ledger, which the reader then classifies as corrupt and REFUSES to append to (silently stalling all future evidence). FIX: write the payload to a temp file in the same dir, then renameSync() over the target (rename(2) is atomic on POSIX) — a crash between the two syscalls leaves the OLD ledger intact; on rename failure the temp is removed and the error rethrown (no orphan, no swallow). HONEST SCOPE (explicit in the code comment, NOT overclaimed): this does NOT serialize two CONCURRENT read-modify-write appenders (the lost-update the S3 recon reproduced) — that remains gated by the one-active-mission governance discipline (no automated path dispatches two missions concurrently; fleet-dispatcher/collector are unlocked operator CLIs) with bounded impact (git-ignored ephemeral evidence, 1 lost entry), and a file-lock is a deferred defense-in-depth. INDEPENDENT AUDIT ⇒ ACCEPT (all 5 points): atomicity EMPIRICALLY PROVEN (monkey-patched rename-throw ⇒ old ledger byte-identical, not torn); no .tmp residue on success; failure rethrows + cleans up; all 5 ledger suites pass (proven-gate/failclosed/controlled/reuse-hook/economic); corrupt-skip + idempotent-duplicate-skip unchanged; honest scope CONFIRMED (lost-update reproduced, still documented, not silently fixed/ignored); no temp-name collision (synchronous single-process; distinct PIDs; stale-orphan harmlessly overwritten). Gate: tsc 0, build 0, full regression 235/235, 0 stale. Register 100 ACCEPTED. The documented SAFE non-owner-gated follow-on queue is now EMPTY. Integration: stacked …→F1c→S3b; NOT merged (gh-auth gate).

items.title: Durable git/GitHub integration preflight: machine-enforced PUSHED≠MERGED≠RELEASED + non-interactive gh-auth detection with exact owner path (prevents the push/merge conflation root-cause)
items.evidence: PR(this cycle, branch excellence/git-integration-preflight-20261030 stacked on the 14-lot tip d4ae7e0): new runtime/bin/odg-integration-preflight.ts + odg-integration-preflight.test.ts + tsconfig.runtime-dist.json (dist include) + package.json (gated). DELIVERABLE for the CTO's root-cause Git/GitHub repair mandate §4. ROOT CAUSE diagnosed with EVIDENCE (forensic, no secrets): git push/fetch authenticate via the SSH key (ssh -T git@github.com ⇒ 'successfully authenticated' — all 14 POST-V107 commits pushed), while PR/merge go through `gh` which needs a SEPARATE GitHub API token that is ABSENT (gh auth status ⇒ not logged in; no ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml; no GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN) — and stdin is NOT a tty in this agent process, so interactive `gh auth login` menus/device-flow cannot be driven here (explains the earlier 'wrong place' confusion). The two auth channels are independent; the campaign conflated 'push succeeded' with 'merged'. There is NO computer-side path to authenticate gh without an owner-supplied credential — a genuine credential gate, not a fixable code defect. TOOL (the durable prevention): pure classifyBranch/authState/planMergeOrder + a thin read-only CLI over `git rev-parse` + `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<b> origin/main` + `gh auth status`. Reports the HONEST per-branch state (LOCAL/PUSHED/MERGED/DIVERGED/ABSENT) using ONLY git (no gh to OBSERVE); NEVER reports MERGED unless the tip is a proven ancestor of origin/main (FAIL-CLOSED — cannot verify ⇒ not merged, no crash); gh-auth detected non-interactively with the EXACT owner command (fine-grained PAT via GH_TOKEN — Contents+Pull-requests RW — the official headless path per cli.github.com/docs.github.com, WebSearch-verified+cited 2026-10-30; or `gh auth login` in the owner tty); plans a linear-stack merge order. REAL run on the live 11 lot branches ⇒ origin/main a8d1c4f, gh NOT AUTHED (+owner cmd), 0 merged / 11 pushed-awaiting-merge, 'NOTHING is RELEASED until merged'. INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL AUDIT ⇒ ACCEPT-WITH-CONCERNS: core purpose PROVEN (no input makes a merely-pushed branch read MERGED; fail-closed strict-boolean; non-vacuous — a mutant that treats pushed-as-merged dies on the test; no network mutation; secret value never printed). THREE honesty/robustness concerns in the tool's own area, ALL CLOSED post-audit + locked by +3 assertions: (1) GH_TOKEN-only was mislabeled 'stored-credential' ⇒ split gh-status from GH_TOKEN + token-precedence label ('GH_TOKEN-env', verified real-run); (2) planMergeOrder infinite-recursion on a cyclic parentTip ⇒ on-stack cycle guard (no RangeError); (3) classifyBranch pure-API now self-enforces 'no remote tip ⇒ never MERGED'. +gated runtime/bin/odg-integration-preflight.test.ts (20, hermetic — injected git runner, no network). Gate: tsc 0, build 0, full regression 236/236, 0 stale. Register 101 ACCEPTED (verified+pushed; itself awaiting the same gh-merge gate). items.title: CI portability of the confined code-checkers: bind node execPath + rust sysroot in the bwrap sandbox; serialize the resource-heavy code-execution suite — closes a local-green/CI-red gap that would also break confined review on rustup/hostedtoolcache production hosts
items.evidence: Found when the 15-lot POST-V107 stack first hit REAL CI after gh auth (it had only ever run locally, where node=/usr/bin/node and rustc sysroot=/usr/lib/rust-* sit under the bound /usr). THREE deterministic CI-only defects, each root-caused + fixed + proven: (1) ts-project-check.ts + code-execution.ts exec process.execPath INSIDE bwrap but bound only /usr,/lib,/lib64,/bin,/sbin ⇒ on GitHub runners node lives in /opt/hostedtoolcache (outside) ⇒ 'execvp: No such file or directory' ⇒ false BLOCKED/FAIL — FIX: ro-bind process.execPath (2d1486d); (2) code-execution runs real go+rustc+tsc compiles (~65s) with a 20s per-compile bound ⇒ under the parallel pool on a 2-core runner a cold confined compile times out ⇒ false FAIL — FIX: HAZARD_ALLOWLIST serialize code-execution (e5dd838); (3) confined rustc on a rustup host (runner rustc 1.99.1) has its sysroot under ~/.rustup (unbound) ⇒ even legit Rust can't find std ⇒ false FAIL — FIX: resolve `rustc --print sysroot`, exec the real <sysroot>/bin/rustc, ro-bind the sysroot with deduped ancestor-aware binds (00c68ef); + an if:failure CI diagnostic (424c82e). Mechanically proven: bwrap exec of an out-of-/usr node fails w/ only sys dirs bound, succeeds w/ the binary bound; all 3 suites pass under a node copied outside /usr. Gate: build:runtime + tsc --noEmit clean; test:report 236/236 local; CI GREEN on 00c68ef (#268) + main 0fdb8bf. NOT a weakening — only toolchain code (node binary, rust sysroot) is additionally exposed; the include!/reference host-read confinement is unchanged. Hardens production too (confined review now works on rustup/hostedtoolcache hosts, not just apt).

items.title: CI-reliability: per-suite SIGKILL process-GROUP timeout in odg-test-report (both runners) + ci.yml step timeout — one hung suite can no longer stall the Classified test gate to the 20-min job kill
items.evidence: Gate-A diagnosis (independent agent) confirmed root cause: odg-test-report had NO per-suite timeout in EITHER runner, so a suite that never exits stalls the whole classified gate until the 20-min job timeout fires CANCELLED (observed recurrently across the POST-V107 campaign; remedy had been manual cancel+rerun). The parallel path (CI default ODG_TEST_WORKERS=8, spawnSuiteAsync) was doubly exposed: a child that never emits close leaves its Promise unresolved -> Promise.all never resolves -> the gate never completes. FIX (mirrors runtime/core/local-test-gate.ts + runtime/bin/odg-schedule-tick.ts SIGKILL-timeout pattern): SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS (env ODG_TEST_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 240000ms ~= 4x slowest real suite ~65s). Both runners spawn with detached:true (new process GROUP) because tsx spawns a grandchild node in the same group — killing only the direct child leaves the grandchild holding the stdout pipe OPEN so close never fires (reproduced empirically). On timeout we SIGKILL the whole GROUP (process.kill(-pid)): defaultRunner (spawnSync timeout+killSignal:SIGKILL, then group-reap the leaked grandchild; verified spawnSync returns promptly ~1509ms despite the grandchild) and spawnSuiteAsync (setTimeout -> killGroup() -> close fires -> Promise resolves). A SIGKILLed suite exits non-zero => classify FAIL (fail-closed), and classify now surfaces the ##SUITE_TIMEOUT marker as the result reason so the report NAMES the hung suite as a timeout, not a bare exit 1. Complementary ci.yml: Classified test gate step timeout-minutes:12 (belt-and-suspenders outer bound; invariant suite 240s < step 12m < job 20m). Regression: odg-test-report.test.ts +7 assertions (hang fixture killed+FAIL+timeout-named via BOTH real runners within a bounded window; happy-path PASS unchanged through the same real runners; 54->61 assertions) incl. a real hanging tsx child driven by a short 1500ms timeout set before module load (isolated to that child process). Full classified gate GREEN: TOTAL 239 PASS 239 FAIL 0 (parallel path, 189s wall, no stall). tsc clean BOTH tsconfigs; build:runtime OK. No change to classification/order for non-hanging suites; no false timeout on fast suites. 9 primitives FROZEN. Pending independent verification + merge. — ACCEPTED: merged PR#306 @f40e3b5 (2 commits: 03b882a per-suite timeout + 378e054 ROOT-CAUSE teardown of external-research-live.test.ts lingering-socket hang). Remote CI GREEN 3m37s; the PRIOR run FAILED, SURFACING the real hang (SUITE_TIMEOUT 240s) — the same hang that CANCELLED main PR#303 while #304/#305 slipped through — which commit 2 fixed. Root cause reproduced deterministically (lingering server socket => srv.close never resolves => process never exits). Independently verified TWICE (timeout feature + teardown fix, separate agents, all points PASS).

items.title: external-research-live CI flake fully closed: httpGetBounded resolve-once + suite watchdog + gate observability + deterministic time-limit assertion
items.evidence: ROOT CAUSE of the residual intermittent gate hang that the #306 teardown fix did NOT fully close (proven: #309 — a doc-only PR off main which INCLUDES #306 — still hit SUITE_TIMEOUT on external-research-live): in runtime/core/capability-executors.ts httpGetBounded, the byte-cap path did `truncated=true; req.destroy()` then relied on a LATER event (res end/error, req error/timeout) to resolve — but a bare req.destroy() emits none of those reliably ⇒ the Promise can hang forever (client-side sibling of the #306 server-socket teardown hang; timing-dependent ⇒ local pass / CI flake). FIX: resolve-once — settle() de-dupes every resolution; the byte-cap resolves IMMEDIATELY (no wait-for-event); added res aborted + a req close LAST-RESORT so the Promise ALWAYS settles even if every other event is missed. This also closes a latent PRODUCTION hang (a byte-capped external-research fetch could hang). EVIDENCE: new hermetic runtime/core/http-get-bounded.test.ts 6/6 (normal; byte-cap on a server that NEVER ends + only dribbles ⇒ must resolve-at-cap, each case under a hard deadline so a regression FAILs not hangs; no-response timeout; connection-refused; bad-proto/invalid-url) run 3× all ~2s; external-research-live 14/14 run 5× all ~2s; wired into test:report gate; tsc clean BOTH; full gate green. Independent verify + CI (re-run to confirm the flake is gone). 9 primitives FROZEN. UPDATE (reality-wins): the resolve-once httpGetBounded fix closes a real latent PRODUCTION fetch hang + one client-side path, but it did NOT by itself green CI — PR#310 CI run-1 passed yet the CONFIRMATORY run-2 STILL hit SUITE_TIMEOUT on external-research-live. A process that runs all 14 assertions but never exits = a LEAKED HANDLE (or unforeseen never-resolving await). Rather than guess a 3rd specific handle, the suite is now DETERMINISTIC + SELF-DIAGNOSING: (1) a ref'd 60s watchdog (well before the 240s gate kill) dumps active handles/requests so CI names the culprit, then exits; (2) after teardown, setImmediate(process.exit(exitCode||0)) forces a clean exit so a post-completion leaked handle can never hang the gate. Verdict is fully determined by the assertions (forcing exit after they run masks nothing); an injected false assertion still exits 1 (FAIL preserved). Opt-out ODG_TEST_NO_WATCHDOG=1. Local: 14/14 x3 ~2s exit0 watchdog-never-fires + fail-copy exit1. Requires 2 green CI runs to accept. FINAL ROOT CAUSE (surfaced by the observability add): after the hang was fixed, #310 still exited 1 — the gate's new FAIL-tail print revealed an AssertionError at external-research-live.test.ts:76 'time limit enforced ... status 0': the toEarly fetch used a 1ms timeout against an INSTANT in-process loopback server, so on a fast CI runner the response completed before 1ms ⇒ status 200 ⇒ flaky. This racy assertion was previously MASKED by the hang. FIX: time-limit enforcement is now DETERMINISTIC — a dedicated server that delays its response 3000ms vs a 100ms fetch deadline, so the deadline always trips ⇒ status 0; the slow server's timer is cleared on socket close and torn down with the can't-hang teardown. ALSO shipped (observability, odg-test-report.ts): the classified gate now prints a bounded stdout tail for FAIL/BLOCKED suites (the assertion error / ##SUITE_WATCHDOG dump) instead of only the suite name — which is what made this diagnosable; gate self-test 61/61. Local external-research-live 14/14 ×5 ~2s exit0 watchdog-never-fires; full gate green. Components: (1) httpGetBounded resolve-once [prod], (2) suite-exit watchdog [determinism+diagnostic], (3) gate FAIL-tail observability, (4) deterministic time-limit assertion [flaky-test fix]. 2 green CI runs required to accept. ACCEPTED: merged PR#310 @e1b5733; two consecutive green CI runs on the final commit + independent verifier PASS; external-research-live CI flake closed (resolve-once + suite watchdog + gate FAIL-tail observability + deterministic time-limit assertion).

items.title: patch-executor applyUnifiedDiff: bound hunk-start to EOF (DoS: oversized hunk header -> OOM/stall in prefix-copy loop)
items.evidence: Recon-confirmed HIGH: applyUnifiedDiff derives hunkStart from the (tool/attacker-controllable) declared old-start line, then runs `while (orig < hunkStart) result.push(origLines[orig++])`. A header like `@@ -999999999,1 @@` against a short file pushes ~1e9 `undefined` entries => memory blowup / multi-second stall (DoS) before the per-line context check can fail. The existing `hunkStart < orig` check guards only the LOWER bound. Fix: one strictly-greater guard `if (hunkStart > origLines.length) throw ...` (a start past EOF cannot apply; `hunkStart === origLines.length` stays legal for an append-at-EOF hunk). The throw is caught by the executor's patch-level catch and recorded FAILED (blocks validation; nothing half-written). Tests: patch-executor.test.ts +5 (now 25): oversized hunk handled <10s, exit 0, recorded FAILED with 'past end of file', no APPLIED entry, target file unmutated; PLUS an append-at-EOF regression (hunkStart === line count) that must still APPLY. build:runtime + tsc(both) green; sibling suites patch-executor-governance-guard 13/13 + symlink-confinement 19/19 green; full gate 243/243.

items.title: nl-objective-gateway: abstain fail-closed on an uncovered-locale objective (close the non-EN/FR/AR under-classification fail-open + fairness gap)
items.evidence: Recon-confirmed MEDIUM (safety under-classification + fairness). The deterministic Risk/External-Effect classifier covers keyword families only for LATIN script (EN + diacritic-folded FR) and ARABIC. An objective written PREDOMINANTLY in any other script (CJK, Cyrillic, Devanagari, Hangul, Hebrew, Greek, Thai, ...) matches no family and fell through to NONE/GENERATE/LOW with requiresHuman=false — the SAME governance fail-open V2-B1 closed for FR/AR, still open for every uncovered locale (and a fairness gap for those users). Fix: new deterministic localeCovered(goal) counts alphabetic code points by Unicode script (\p{Script=Latin}/\p{Script=Arabic} vs any other \p{L}) and returns false only when an uncovered script is the STRICT majority of the letters. classifyObjective now returns localeCovered on every verdict: a matched family ⇒ true (the dangerous keyword was found regardless of script); NONE + covered ⇒ the existing safe LOW verdict (localeCovered true, unchanged); NONE + uncovered ⇒ requiresHuman:true + localeCovered:false (could-not-classify, not a safety proof). compile() adds an UNCOVERED_LOCALE blocker when localeCovered===false ⇒ status BLOCKED / recovery ABSTAIN (fail-closed, dry-run, zero side effects). Over-classification toward human review is the safe direction. DOCUMENTED LIMITATION (not silently closed): a Latin-script language we lack keywords for (e.g. Spanish 'borra el archivo') is indistinguishable from English by script alone and remains a keyword gap; closing it needs a probabilistic language detector (non-deterministic), out of scope. Tests: nl-objective-gateway.test.ts block 32 (+13 => 252 assertions): CJK/Cyrillic ⇒ localeCovered false + requiresHuman true + NONE; EN/FR/AR benign NOT flagged; Arabic DESTRUCTIVE still classified (coverage never downgrades a matched family); mixed Latin-dominant stays covered; compile uncovered ⇒ UNCOVERED_LOCALE blocker + BLOCKED/ABSTAIN + no side effects; covered EN/AR compile ⇒ no blocker. build:runtime + tsc(both) green; full gate 243/243.

items.title: ollama-provider loopbackGet response-size cap (parity with loopbackPost; bound unbounded local-daemon body)
items.evidence: Recon-confirmed LOW-MED dos. loopbackGet (used by detectOllama for /api/tags discovery) accumulated data += c with NO byte cap, while loopbackPost enforces a 2MB cap and the file header explicitly promises 'a bounded timeout + response-size cap'. A daemon — or any process that grabbed loopback :11434 — streaming an unbounded body would be buffered entirely in memory (OOM/DoS); the 5s timeout does not bound bytes received within the window. Fix: mirror loopbackPost exactly — track bytes += c.length, on bytes>maxBytes call req.destroy()+finish({ok:false,reason:'response exceeded size cap'}); maxBytes opt defaults 2_000_000. Host/port stay HARDCODED (loopback-only, no SSRF surface); added a test-only injectable request-FUNCTION seam (not host/port), consistent with the existing get/post transport seams, and exported loopbackGet. Tests: ollama-provider.test.ts +3 (now 18): over-cap ⇒ ok:false 'response exceeded size cap'; under-cap ⇒ ok:true parsed; default 2MB generous. build:runtime + tsc(both) green; consumers ollama-control-plane-contract 10/10 + coding-executor 9/9 green; full gate 243/243.

items.title: Bound external input before regex (ReDoS defense-in-depth): third-party-agent-gate validateParams no-continue + dataset-quality cellConforms cap

ODG evolution-loop BASELINE_COMPARE evaluates ONE candidate at a time vs the static baseline and forwards each independently (grep-verified: no tournament/selectBest/incumbent selection). runtime/core/champion-challenger-arbiter.ts adds N-way comparative selection COMPOSING improvement-baseline.measureDelta + meta-intelligence.assessIntegrity + compounding-loop.rewardHackingCheck + evaluator-independence.auditIndependence: disqualify any challenger regressing ANY champion metric, or failing integrity (DETECTED/SUSPECTED), reward-hacking, or independence (COMPROMISED); pick the largest clean lift (stable id tie-break); no survivor strictly beats => KEEP_CHAMPION. selfAuthorized:false, grantsNoPromotion:true — promotion stays EXTERNAL via evolution-loop.applyExternalPromotion. PROVEN: 12/12 tests. tsc clean; in test:report. No new engine; takes no promotion decision.

items.title: SÉRIE 22 P13: quantization honesty gate (speedup accepted only within declared accuracy tolerance)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (research-agent-found gap): the 2026 inference-optimization norm is that a quantized model speed/cost win is valid ONLY when a declared task-specific accuracy-degradation tolerance is met (arXiv 2411.02355v4 2026: FP8 lossless, INT8 ~1-3%, INT4 ~1-15%+; Traversaal.ai 2026: accept if MMLU drop <1.5% / GSM8K <2% else QAT). ODG had the speed side (inference-engine.benchmark) + the quality side (p2-passk-reliability.passAtK) but NOTHING tied one to the other (grep-verified: no quantiz/int8/fp8/perplexity module). runtime/core/quantization-honesty-gate.ts composes both: ACCEPT only when a measured speedup/cost win AND held-out pass^k accuracy drop <= DECLARED tolerance AND reliability (flakiness) regression <= tolerance; accuracy drop beyond tolerance => REFUSED_REGRESSION; a speedup claim with NO held-out rollouts => INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (never credited); no win => NO_WIN. Pure/deterministic (no network/GPU/clock/random); missing tolerance => 0 (strict). PROVEN 10/10. tsc clean; in test:report. No new engine.

items.title: SÉRIE 22 eval-integrity: statistical significance/uncertainty (Wilson CI + two-proportion z + McNemar)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (research-agent-found gap): 2026 reporting standards require every eval claim to carry sampling uncertainty (STREAM arXiv 2508.09853 Aug-2026: must include a confidence interval or SE; rank-interval papers 2606.08679/2607.16259 2026: overlapping CIs cannot determine which model is better). ODG computed point estimates everywhere (capability-taxonomy.computeVerifiedSuccessRate even emits the literal unfulfilled string report-confidence-interval) but NO module attached an error bar or tested a delta vs noise (grep-verified absent). runtime/core/eval-significance.ts supplies closed-form (no bootstrap/random/clock): wilsonInterval (fulfils that TODO), twoProportionZ (unpaired diff-CI + z), mcnemarPaired (paired same-cases test), significanceGate (a delta is an IMPROVEMENT only if statistically significant AND positively directed, else INCONCLUSIVE; n=0 => NO_DATA, never fabricated). Verified vs known values (Wilson 18/20 = [0.699,0.972]; McNemar b=0 c=8 chi2=6.125 significant; 9/10->10/10 = INCONCLUSIVE noise). WIRED into champion-challenger-arbiter (optional, backward-compatible): a directional lift carrying sampled eval evidence must be significant to qualify, closing the direction-only forwarding weakness. PROVEN 17/17 (+arbiter 15/15). tsc clean; in test:report. No new engine.

items.title: SÉRIE 22 P12: dead-letter / poison-pill quarantine (retry budget + head-of-line)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (research-agent-found gap): the 2026 poison-message best practice (OneUptime 2026-01-21; DLQ Production Guide 2026) — a permanently-failing record blocks every higher offset; after a finite retry budget (3-5) it is routed to a dedicated dead-letter partition, NEVER retried forever and NEVER silently dropped; transient must be separated from permanent. ODG P12 covered ordering/dedup/replay/backpressure/watermark late-drop but had NO failure-based quarantine (grep-verified: no dead-letter/poison/DLQ, no attempt budget; p12-watermark drops LATE events = a TIME property, orthogonal to UN-PROCESSABLE = a FAILURE property). runtime/core/p12-dead-letter-quarantine.ts partitions deliveries into DELIVERED/RETRYING/DEAD_LETTERED: attempts>=budget OR invalid/missing attempt count => DEAD_LETTERED (poison, fail-closed); for ordered streams the lowest-seq RETRYING record is the head-of-line blocker and quarantining poison unblocks it. Composes p12-watermark house-style + idempotency-guard (dead-lettered id never re-admitted) + p15-saga-compensation. Pure (no broker/clock/network). PROVEN 12/12. tsc clean; in test:report. No new engine.

items.title: SÉRIE 22 P8: API deprecation-window / sunset enforcement (deprecate-before-remove)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (research-agent-found gap): 2026 API-sunset discipline (OneUptime 2026-02-02; RFC 9745 Deprecation header + RFC 8594 Sunset) requires an element be ANNOUNCED deprecated BEFORE removal, with a grace window, never removed silently. ODG P8 enforced version-bump SEVERITY (p8-semver-enforcement: breaking=>MAJOR) and DETECTED breaking removals (api-contract.checkCompatibility) but NOT deprecate-before-removal: a publisher could yank a required output in one MAJOR jump with zero window (grep-verified absent: no sunset/grace-window/deprecation-window on API contracts; the only deprecat* hits are unrelated mission-governance states). runtime/core/p8-deprecation-window-enforcement.ts composes both P8 modules VERBATIM: a backward-incompatible removal/type-change is ADMITTED only if the element was marked deprecated in the PRIOR contract AND the semver bump is OK; a breaking removal of a NON-deprecated element => SUNSET_VIOLATION even when MAJOR is correct; missing deprecated list => deny-by-default; insufficient bump forwarded as SEMVER_VIOLATION. Pure/deterministic, no second diff/semver engine. PROVEN 8/8. tsc clean; in test:report. No new engine.

items.title: SÉRIE 23 central-intelligence: calibration trust gate (ECE Act-Ask-Abstain before confidence drives a decision)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (research-agent-found gap): 2026 agentic standard (CAAG IJCOPE 2026-05; I-CALM arXiv 2604.03904; Stable-Miscalibration 2608.13591) — confidence may drive an autonomous decision ONLY if empirically calibrated (ECE target <0.05), else ask/abstain; raw confidence is systematically overconfident. ODG could MEASURE calibration (eval-metrics.reliabilityBins/brierScore) but NO module turned it into a verdict or gated a decision (grep-verified: no ECE/calibrationError consumer; arbiter/p11-routing/cognitive-decision trust raw confidence). runtime/core/calibration-trust-gate.ts composes eval-metrics (ECE = sample-weighted bin reliability gap, no new primitive) + meta-intelligence.assessIntegrity: CALIBRATED (ECE<=target, n>=minSamples, no high-bin overconfidence, integrity clean) => ACT; OVERCONFIDENT/MISCALIBRATED => ASK_OR_ABSTAIN; NO_DATA (few samples) / UNTRUSTED (integrity DETECTED/SUSPECTED) => ABSTAIN (deny-by-default). selfAuthorized:false, grants no authority. Pure closed-form. PROVEN 10/10. tsc clean; in test:report. No new engine.

items.title: SÉRIE 23 security: tool-definition integrity gate (MCP tool-poisoning / rug-pull)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (research-agent-found gap): NSA/DoD MCP advisory (2026-06-02) + OWASP MCP Top-10 (2026) + mcp-scan tool-pinning — an external tool advertised definition is an attack surface: TOOL POISONING (injection in the description read at planning time) and RUG PULL (silent post-approval mutation). ODG pinned the ODG-side contract and vetted the agent PROPOSAL but never pinned/scanned the external tool definition (grep-verified: no tool-pinning/descriptionHash/rug-pull/MCP). runtime/core/tool-definition-integrity-gate.ts runs upstream of third-party-agent-gate: composes evidence-provenance.contentDigest (pin) + frontier-radar.sanitizeExternal (poison scan) + an external-approval predicate (mirrors root-of-trust.externallyElevated, internal): no baseline => DENY_UNPINNED; digest changed with no external re-approval => DENY_RUG_PULL; injection in description => DENY_TOOL_POISONING; (re-)pin ONLY via external approval (not self). Pure/deterministic, deny-by-default. PROVEN 9/9. tsc clean; in test:report. No new engine.

items.title: SÉRIE 23 reliability: circuit breaker (CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN with recovery probe)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (research-agent-found gap): circuit-breaker recovery pattern (Azure Arch Center; resilience4j; Resilient Microservices arXiv 2512.16959 2025) — trip OPEN on failure-rate, HALF_OPEN after cooldown admits bounded probes, re-CLOSE only if probes succeed (any probe failure re-opens). ODG had DLQ/saga/burn-rate/watermark but NO circuit breaker (grep-verified: no HALF_OPEN/circuit/breaker state machine; third-party-agent-gate circuit-break is a one-way budget cap). runtime/core/p12-circuit-breaker.ts composes p7-burn-rate-alert.burnRate (failure-rate-over-threshold trip) + the DLQ outcome vocabulary; CLOSED trips only at >=minSamples (resilience4j min-calls); OPEN short-circuits until caller-supplied cooldown ticks elapse (no clock); HALF_OPEN any probe FAIL re-opens, probeLimit clean probes close; fail-closed: unknown state/invalid outcome => OPEN. An OPEN breaker stops RETRYING records storming the p12-dead-letter-quarantine. PROVEN 11/11. tsc clean; in test:report. No new engine.

items.title: SÉRIE 23/W8 P12: idempotency-key collision detection (same key, different payload)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (research-agent-found gap): IETF httpapi Idempotency-Key draft — a key presented with a request whose fingerprint DIFFERS from the stored one MUST be rejected (422), never replayed; 2026 payment-API guidance corroborates. ODG idempotency-guard.admit + event-stream-engine.publish both dedup on the KEY STRING only and store no request fingerprint, so a reused key with a different payload is silently reconciled to the original result (grep-verified absent: no idempotency collision/fingerprint/mismatch). runtime/core/p12-idempotency-key-collision.ts composes state-transition.canonicalize (key-order-independent fingerprint, no new hashing primitive) + idempotency-guard DUPLICATE/never-overwrite semantics: same key + matching fingerprint => DUPLICATE (safe replay); different fingerprint => COLLISION (reject, never replay); missing key / stored-entry-without-fingerprint => COLLISION (fail-closed). Pure/deterministic. PROVEN 7/7. tsc clean; in test:report. No new engine.

items.title: V5 Phase 3 / RCE-04: Root-Cause Intelligence (causal-layer classifier)

items.title: V5 Phase 4 / M-CH3-03: RCE Independent Assurance chain (RETAIN/ROLLBACK/NEEDS_REVIEW)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (Master program §4.4 + RCE-07/RCE-08): runtime/core/rce-assurance-chain.ts enforces the obligatory repair chain before a fix is kept — FAIL-TO-PASS (reproduction FAILED before, PASSES after), PASS-TO-PASS (previously-passing tests still pass, no regression), ADVERSARIAL (survives probing), INDEPENDENT VERIFY (verifier independent of builder, reuses evaluator-independence.auditIndependence). Decision RETAIN only if all gates pass; a pass-to-pass regression or adversarial failure => ROLLBACK; COMPROMISED independence / incomplete evidence / invalid reproduction => NEEDS_REVIEW. The fix is NEVER its own proof. Fail-closed: missing evidence => NEEDS_REVIEW, never RETAIN on an unproven fix. Decides whether to keep an evidence bundle; applies/reverts nothing. PROVEN 9/9; tsc clean; in test:report. COMPLETED, not yet VALIDATED. Deps on rce-root-cause-intelligence (diagnosis precedes assurance).

items.title: V5-E Engineering Intelligence: E-COLDSTART measurement + model (unsafe bundle REJECTED)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (Engineering Intelligence E-COLDSTART): measured tsx per-suite cold-start = 1.85s (node 0.18s) = ~95% of each suite cost; test bodies ~0.05s. Reconciled the ~727s cumulative estimate with the real 187s gate: 369 x 1.85s = 683s serial, parallelized across 8 cores => ~187s; worker scaling flattens beyond cores (W=4 8.67s, W=10 6.77s on 20 suites). ADVERSARIAL RESULT: the obvious esbuild-bundle+node shortcut (~0.17s/suite, ~11x) is REJECTED_UNSAFE — a failing assert.ok(false) bundled+run on node exited 0 (SWALLOWED the failure) AND broke the dual CJS/ESM export interop (selectValidation is not a function). A speed win that masks a failure is forbidden (section 4) — NOT adopted. runtime/core/coldstart-model.ts encodes this: projectGate/compareStrategies gate a strategy ADOPTION on correctnessPreserved===true (speed never excuses masking), cap workers at cores, recommend cores-1. Honest conclusion: the safe demonstrated win is test-impact selection (validation-selector ~97%) + worker cap; no correctness-preserving tsx replacement proven yet. PROVEN 9/9; tsc clean; in test:report; findings in docs/odg/VALIDATION_CHAIN_BASELINE.md. COMPLETED, not yet VALIDATED.

items.title: V5-E wave-2: persistent file-level impact graph (provenance + invalidation)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-08 (Engineering Intelligence wave-2 task 2): runtime/core/persistent-impact-graph.ts adds PERSISTENCE + PROVENANCE + automatic INVALIDATION on top of the existing change-impact-graph (no concurrent graph — the graph IS change-impact-graph.buildGraph, injected). items.title: V12.4 Architecture Intelligence & Rationalization: read-only architectural audit (cycles/duplication/unused, responsibilities-not-names)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-09 (V12.4 Architecture Intelligence & Rationalization — read-only audit #1, addendum §3-§5): runtime/core/architecture-audit.ts is a PURE read-only architectural analyzer. It REUSES the existing dependency graph (change-impact-graph.buildGraph) — no new graph/engine (anti-gas-factory). It detects (a) circular dependencies (cycle-safe DFS), (b) EXACT responsibility duplications by comparing RESPONSIBILITIES (contract domain + sorted exported-symbol set), NOT file names, and (c) unused components (no static consumer + no test + not an entrypoint). Every candidate is NEEDS_REVIEW — a similarity NEVER authorizes a fusion; a RETIRE needs independent proof of zero remaining dependencies (§5/§7). PROVEN 13/13; tsc clean; in test:report. LIVE audit over 426 runtime/core modules (docs/odg/ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_V12.4.md): 0 circular deps, 0 exact duplications; 7 unused flags ALL verified FALSE POSITIVES (static graph under-approximates dynamic/string/contract-test edges) — honestly reported, nothing merged/retired/changed. Read-only; it grants no authority.

items.title: V12.4 Engineering Throughput Optimization: baseline + coherent delivery lots (fewer CI waits, identical controls)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-09 (V12.4 Engineering Throughput Optimization — baseline + coherent-delivery-lots, §3/§5/§9/§11): reproducible throughput baseline (docs/odg/THROUGHPUT_BASELINE_V12.4.md) measured with EXISTING instruments (gate-instrumentation.statsOf/decompose/speedupTarget + performance-observability.compareReproducible) — NO new measurement engine (anti-gas-factory). Measured data: tsx cold-start 1.59-1.87s; one real suite 1.66-1.75s (~95% startup); CI wall-clock 244-246s per delivery (real runs PR#413/#414); FULL gate ~187s/383 suites. #1 bottleneck = per-PR serial CI wait ~245s (paid once per delivery). Justified improvement runtime/core/delivery-batch-coherence.ts: groups technically-RELATED missions (shared write-set OR dep edge OR shared impacted module via change-impact-graph) into one coherent delivery ⇒ pay CI once instead of k times, IDENTICAL controls (same FULL gate runs once; no suite skipped; no assertion removed; no NOT_RUN as PASS). Fail-closed: independent missions MUST_SEPARATE (never grouped — regression risk, §5); no-write-set never batched; over-large related group split (bounded blast radius). Gain is a CI-wait COUNT (k-1 saved per proven lot), NOT a promised % (§9). PROVEN 15/15; tsc clean; in test:report.

items.title: V5 Phase 2 / M-CH2-01: 15 trades per-métier baseline + gap inventory (read-only, no métier-logic rewrite)
items.evidence: ODG-accepted 2026-11-09 (V5 PHASE-2 M-CH2-01 — 15 trades per-métier baseline + gap inventory): runtime/core/metier-baseline.ts is a PURE READ-ONLY rollup that does NOT rewrite any métier internal business logic (directive exclusion). It COMPOSES the existing multidimensional métier benchmark (metier-benchmark-multidim.runMultidim: DETECTION/SPECIFICITY/ROBUSTNESS per métier) into a per-métier baseline over the full roster P1..P15 and inventories GAPS honestly. LIVE result: 10/15 métiers benchmarked AND effective (P1,P2,P3,P4,P6,P7,P8,P9,P12,P15; detection 1.0, specificity 1.0, reproducible); 5 métiers NOT_BENCHMARKED => GAPS (P5,P10,P11,P13,P14) — never counted as passing (fail-closed); a benchmarked métier that fails any dimension (e.g. a block-everything guard failing SPECIFICITY) is a GAP not a pass; honest maturity L3_VALIDATED only for effective+reproducible, else capped. PROVEN 11/11; tsc clean; in test:report. Read-only; grants no authority.
